annotations.text: First visit to a piece. Sections and variations both invite with the dashed add row the empty variations card already uses. Keys on a piece is one quiet row: rare, but the core allows it.

Rows in score order. A named section shows its bars beneath; a nameless tricky spot is labelled by its bars and carries the highlighter tag, the one bright colour, because a spot is literally highlighted bars. A target tempo shows only when set.
Tap a row to edit. One sheet does add, rename, bars, kind, target tempo and remove; Save sends the whole list once (UpdateSections). Blank tempo reads as the piece's own.
Bars is one text field: musicians type or dictate "bars 5 to 12", and the core parses it. A refusal keeps the sheet open, marks the field and says how to fix it. Wording comes from the core.
Reorder puts the list in edit mode: drag to match the score, minus to remove. Removing hides the section; plays that name it stay readable.

Keys keep the ring scroller exactly as today, now as their own card. Variations sit beneath as rows. VoiceOver reads every ring as the name then the same caption as a row: "F sharp major, Not yet played" (#1925).

Choose opens the key wheel from the item's Key field (KeyPicker), same rings, fills, labels and spelling arrows, now taking several keys (#1769). All major fills the outer ring; the hub counts instead of naming one key.

Each spoke cycles: off, then the circle's spelling, then the other spelling where the spoke has one, then off. A chosen F sharp leads its spoke, G flat drops to the arrow line, exactly as the single picker does.
One list for the whole library. Typing filters it; a new label offers Add. Matches show where they are already used, so a musician reuses rather than duplicates.
